title: Machine learning selected fractionally doped perovskites for synthesis
summary: A function-confined gradient-boosting model trained on 632 records was used to rank fractionally doped perovskite oxides for a solar thermochemical hydrogen-production application. The authors synthesized 11 selected compositions, seven of which the model classified as relevant to that application. This is a composition-discovery and synthesis result; it does not show that all seven were experimentally validated for hydrogen-production performance.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature publisher record and full article author manuscript; composition synthesis separated from predicted application relevance.

evidence.tested: The authors report synthesizing 11 model-selected fractionally doped perovskite oxide compositions; seven were classified as relevant to solar thermochemical hydrogen production. The model was evaluated on 632 training records and achieved reported 95.4% accuracy; this classification metric is not a performance result for the 11 synthesized materials.
evidence.unknown: The evidence reviewed does not establish experimentally measured hydrogen-production performance for all seven materials. The entry does not claim each composition is novel outside the authors’ checked data or that model accuracy generalizes beyond the reported dataset.
evidence.ai_role: A function-confined gradient-boosting classifier ranked compositions for synthesis based on target application criteria.
